name: mcp-ticket-demo

tools.name: search_tickets
tools.description: Find support tickets by status, requester email, or a keyword in subject/body. Call this tool when someone asks to list, find, or search tickets. Do not use list_schemas, get_schema, or run_query for that. Default status is open — an empty list means no match, not an empty server; broaden to status=all. Do not retry the same filters. One known id is get_ticket or ticket://TCK-1001.

status.description: Lifecycle filter. Default open. Use all if a search comes back empty.

requester_email.description: Optional exact customer email, e.g. ada@example.com. Combine with status=all if you are unsure the ticket is still open.

query.description: Optional keyword matched against subject and body, e.g. hostname or mcp.json.

limit.description: Max rows to return. Default 10, max 25.

tools.name: create_ticket
tools.description: Open a support ticket on behalf of a customer. ALWAYS pass requester_email as the real customer email. If you omit it the call still succeeds (201) but the service account owns the ticket and every reply is mailed to the bot, not the customer — that is the attribution scar. A tool is not done when the API call succeeds; it is done when the next thing that happens is right. This is a write tool and may require a credential.

subject.description: Required. Short customer-facing subject, e.g. Cannot find the deployed MCP URL.

body.description: Required. What happened, in the customer's words.

requester_email.description: The real customer's email, e.g. ada@example.com. Omit ONLY to reproduce the attribution scar.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to an existing ticket. You need a real ticket_id from search_tickets or get_ticket — do not invent TCK- ids. Pass author as the human speaking; omitting it attributes the comment to the service account. This is a write tool and may require a credential. To resolve the ticket after commenting, call close_ticket.

ticket_id.description: Existing ticket id from search_tickets or get_ticket. Format: TCK-1001. Do not invent an id.

body.description: The comment text the human wants on the ticket.

author.description: Email of the person speaking, e.g. ada@example.com. Omit only if you intend to comment as the service account.

tools.name: close_ticket
tools.description: Resolve and close a support ticket (destructive, idempotent). Sets status to solved and records resolved_at. Optionally appends resolution as the final comment. If the ticket is already solved this is a no-op and returns alreadyClosed=true — do not retry. Use a real ticket_id from search_tickets or get_ticket. Use add_comment first if you want a longer explanation before closing. This is a write tool and may require a credential.

ticket_id.description: Existing ticket id from search_tickets or get_ticket. Format: TCK-1001. Do not invent an id.

resolution.description: Optional note appended as the final comment, e.g. Fixed by using an absolute cwd in mcp.json.

closed_by.description: Who is closing, e.g. support@example.com. Defaults to the service account.

tools.name: get_ticket
tools.description: Fetch one ticket by id, including comments and attribution (customer vs service_account). Call this tool when you have an id like TCK-1001. If you do not have an id, call search_tickets. Do not call get_schema with name ticket, and do not use run_query, to read one ticket. Same data is at ticket://TCK-1001.

ticket_id.description: Existing ticket id from search_tickets. Format: TCK-1001. Do not invent an id.

tools.name: list_schemas
tools.description: List names for get_schema. Each row has kind. data = object shape (ticket, customer, settings, server) — call the tool named in the description. query = tickets, customers, or assets — the only names run_query accepts. tool = that tool's arguments — call the tool; this list does not run it. There is no query_tickets tool.

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Read the shape of one name from list_schemas. This does not perform the task. kind=query (tickets, customers, assets): those filterable keys are for run_query. kind=tool: these are the arguments — call that tool next, and do not pass the tool name to run_query. kind=data: an object shape — call the tool named in next. An unknown name is an error.

name.description: Exact name from list_schemas. tickets, customers, or assets are for run_query. A tool name such as search_tickets only returns arguments — then call the tool. ticket, customer, settings, and server are shapes, not queries.

tools.name: run_query
tools.description: Exact-match rows for schema tickets, customers, or assets only. Call search_tickets to find tickets, get_ticket to read one id, and lookup_customer to read one customer — this tool does not replace them. Do not pass a tool name or a singular data name. Do not invent query_tickets or query_with_filter. Empty rows mean no match; loosen the filter, do not retry the same query.

schema.description: tickets, customers, or assets only. Not ticket, customer, settings, server, and not a tool name such as search_tickets.

filter.description: Optional exact-match map. Keys must be listed in get_schema.filterable. Example: {"status":"open"}.

fields.description: Optional field projection. Example: ["id","subject"]. Omit to return all fields.

limit.description: Max rows to return. Default 10, max 50.

tools.name: lookup_customer
tools.description: Look up one customer by email (plan, region, contact). Call this tool for that. run_query schema=customers is a bulk exact match, not this lookup. Tickets use search_tickets. Phone is PII: it stays REDACTED unless the caller presents a credential with the pii scope. Known demo emails: ada@example.com, sam@example.com. Do not invent other addresses and retry.

email.description: Customer email. Demo records: ada@example.com, sam@example.com.

tools.name: describe_server
tools.description: Call this first, and again after any denial or empty tool list: server identity, auth mode, who the server thinks you are, the scopes you hold, your rate-limit budget, and every tool with the scope it needs and whether it is currently available. The tools list is the set of actions — call a tool to do the work, do not get_schema it first. Discovery stays open in every auth mode. When a call was denied, this tells you which credential is missing — do not guess.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: Read the saved settings, including version. Does not return API keys or passwords. Call this before update_settings, and after import_settings or set_ui_auth.

tools.name: update_settings
tools.description: Change several settings in one call. Omit a field to leave it. Then call get_settings. Requires admin even when auth mode is off, because it can change auth mode, rate limit, audit, and the page lock.

rateLimitEnabled.description: true or false. The string "0" is false.

audit.description: Record a call trace when true.

uiAuth.description: Hide desk HTML until sign-in when true.

tools.name: set_auth_mode
tools.description: Set auth mode to off, write, or all. Requires an admin credential even when auth mode is off. Then call describe_server.

tools.name: set_rate_limit
tools.description: Set the per-principal rate limit: enabled, limit, and windowSeconds. The string "0" means false. Requires admin. Then call describe_server.

enabled.description: true or false. The string "0" is false.

tools.name: set_audit
tools.description: Turn the call trace on or off. Requires admin. Then call generate_traffic, then export_log.

enabled.description: true records the trace. "0" is false.

tools.name: set_tool_gate
tools.description: Enable or disable one tool except describe_server. Requires admin. Then call describe_server and read that tool's available field.

tool.description: A tool name from describe_server. Not describe_server.

enabled.description: true or false. The string "0" is false.

tools.name: set_tool_lock
tools.description: Require a credential for one tool except describe_server, even when auth mode is off. Requires admin. Then call describe_server.

tool.description: A tool name from describe_server. Not describe_server.

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: List usernames and scopes. Passwords are never returned. Requires admin even when auth mode is off.

tools.name: create_user
tools.description: Create a user. The password is stored as a hash and is never listed. The built-in admin cannot be replaced. Requires admin.

username.description: New username. Not the built-in admin.

password.description: Password. Stored as a hash, returned nowhere.

scopes.description: Comma-separated scopes: read, write, pii, admin. Default read,write.

tools.name: delete_user
tools.description: Delete a user by username. The built-in admin cannot be removed. Requires admin.

username.description: Username from list_users. Not the built-in admin.

tools.name: list_api_keys
tools.description: List API keys: id, prefix, label, scopes, and active. The secret is never listed. Requires admin.

tools.name: issue_api_key
tools.description: Issue an API key. The secret is returned once in key and is not stored. Requires admin. Then call list_api_keys and confirm the secret is absent.

tools.name: revoke_api_key
tools.description: Revoke an API key by id from list_api_keys or issue_api_key. Requires admin.

tools.name: export_settings
tools.description: Export settings as a document. Omits API keys, the admin password, and any broker password. Pass document to import_settings, then call get_settings.

tools.name: import_settings
tools.description: Restore a document from export_settings. Does not restore API keys or passwords. Then call get_settings.

document.description: The document field from export_settings. kind must be mcp-ticket-demo-settings.

tools.name: export_log
tools.description: Export counters, errors, and the trace. Requires admin. Turn set_audit on and call generate_traffic first if you need a non-empty trace.

tools.name: generate_traffic
tools.description: Record one or more probe rounds in the log. Any credential works, even when auth mode is off. Does not create tickets or change settings. Then call export_log.

rounds.description: How many probe rounds to record. Default 1.

tools.name: set_protocols
tools.description: Set stdio, streamableHttp, and sse. Send all three booleans. At least one must stay true. Requires admin. Then call describe_server.

stdio.description: true or false. The string "0" is false.

tools.name: set_ui_auth
tools.description: Hide desk HTML until an admin signs in. Tool calls stay up. /icon.svg stays public so the login page can show it. Requires admin. Then call get_settings.

enabled.description: true or false. The string "0" is false.

stderr: mcp-ticket-demo stdio — no port, no URL. Secrets stay in env. auth mode=off
